body.contractNote: This integer moves when a field is removed or renamed, or when the meaning of a value changes. Adding a field does not move it, so a caller reading known fields is safe across additions. Pin it, and treat an unexpected value as a reason to stop rather than to guess.
contractOmissions: No confidence figure. There is no number expressing how sure Trooth is about a fact, per fact or overall. Trooth deleted its single composite figure on purpose and a per-fact confidence is the same idea at a smaller scale. A caller that needs one is being asked to invent it, and should not.

No adjudication between disagreeing sources. `conflicts` shows what each source said and picks none of them. There is no winner field, no preferred source, and the order accounts are listed in is the origin vocabulary's fixed order rather than a ranking. Deciding between two accounts is a judgment about the company and Trooth does not make it for a caller.
No completeness signal. An empty list means the company published nothing under that heading. It does not mean Trooth looked everywhere.

No consistency check behind an empty `conflicts`. It lists facts for which two recorded accounts disagree. An empty list means no two recorded accounts of the same fact disagree. It does not mean Trooth compared every declaration with the company's policies, its other pages or the world, and a declaration can be stale or scoped differently from another page without appearing here.

Partial per-claim provenance. Each fact carries who stated or observed it. A company statement carries claim.declaredAt, the time an authorized publish on Trooth first carried its current value or, later, an owner or admin declared every published fact again, only when that publish happened after Trooth began recording it; an older fact unchanged and not declared again has none. A declared fact carries claim.evidenceRef when the company cited a reference, which Trooth has not opened. No fact carries a validity interval, and no fact inherits the reading's time. A fact without a date has no known date. Contract 1 carries none of these fields.

No merging of equivalent wordings. "US" and "United States" are published as a disagreement rather than reconciled, because deciding two phrasings mean the same thing is an interpretation and making it quietly is how a disagreement disappears.

No signature on the public read as a whole. The one signed part is `witnessStatement`, and it is present only when the reading behind `witnessed` was signed under Trooth's witness statement; for an older reading the field is absent and nothing in this response is signed. When it is present, `witnessStatement.payload` is the exact string Trooth signed, `signature` is an Ed25519 signature over its UTF-8 bytes, and `key_id` names the key to check it with at https://api.trooth.co/public/keys. That payload holds the facts of one reading and no verdict. A `trooth.witness-statement.v2` payload also binds the check mapping digest, the evaluator version, the subject scope and the evidence manifest digest (the manifest is carried as `witnessEvidenceManifest`); a v1 payload binds none of these. Every other field, `witnessed`, `facts` and `conflicts` included, is unsigned and should not be read as signed. Trooth signs what it witnessed. It never signs on a company's behalf.

coverage.definition: Counted from the signed witness statement for this reading: checksRun is the checks read in this reading, checksPassed is those whose outcome was as expected, checksNotAsExpected is those read whose outcome was not as expected, and checksNotRead is the entries listed but not read in this reading (self-attestations carried from an earlier reading, and probes that could not be read). Two identities hold: checksInReading = checksRun + checksNotRead, and checksRun = checksPassed + checksNotAsExpected. checksPassed is part of checksRun, not a third addend. A not-read entry is not a negative finding: a timeout or an unavailable source is not read, never not as expected.

signing.subject: One reading Trooth took of this company's public surface: each check's id, category, kind, observed outcome and reason, the counts, the subject scope, the evaluator version, and the digests of the exact check mapping and of the evidence manifest. It does not cover the company's declarations, the facts array, or any other field of this response.

binding.assurance: A v2 statement binds these outcome bytes together with the digest of the exact check mapping, the evaluator version, the subject scope and the digest of the evidence manifest. It does not establish the company's identity, an independently established time, or anything the reading did not read.

signing.keyPurpose: Signing Trooth's readings. The same key signs the directory receipt; it signs nothing on a company's behalf.
signing.timeSource: Asserted by Trooth when it signed. There is no external timestamp or anchor.

methodology.cadence: Continuity readings are attempted every 1 hour.
methodology.gapTolerance: A series is treated as unbroken while readings stay within 3 hours of each other.
methodology.retention: Readings are kept for 400 days, then pruned.
exclusions: Company-declared fields are published as the company wrote them. Trooth does not check them against anything and a date beside one is the date it was written or last edited, not an observation.
Certifications, audit reports and insurance are read as documents where a document exists. Trooth does not contact an auditor, a certification body or an insurer.
No probe reaches inside a product. Readings cover surfaces a domain publishes to the internet and nothing behind an authenticated boundary.
Latency and uptime are not measured. A status-page link is a link.
A reading covers the endpoint that was read at the moment it was read. It does not cover other regions, other endpoints, or the traffic path from anywhere in particular.
Nothing here is a certification, an audit opinion, or a statement that a vendor is safe to buy from.
methodology.summary: Continuity readings are attempted every 1 hour; a series counts as unbroken while readings stay within 3 hours; readings are kept for 400 days. Freshness windows differ by category and are listed with this export. Company-declared fields are not checked, nothing is probed behind an authenticated boundary, and latency and uptime are not measured.

factFreshnessStatuses.current: A dated observation inside its category's freshness window.
factFreshnessStatuses.due: A dated observation near the end of its category's freshness window.
factFreshnessStatuses.stale: A dated observation past its category's freshness window. It describes the past, not the present.
factFreshnessStatuses.not_collected: The company's own statement. Trooth records it and does not re-read it, so its age is not measured.
factFreshnessStatuses.unknown: No per-fact observation time is recorded, or the fact's date cannot be read unambiguously.

evidenceClasses.company_declaration: The company stated it. Trooth records the statement and does not establish it.
evidenceClasses.trooth_observation: Trooth read it itself, from the public surface or from a system the company connected. Which of the two, the resources read and the read time are not yet recorded per fact.
evidenceClasses.public_record: A named public or registry source stated it.

claimFieldMeanings.declaredAt: The time of the authorized publish on Trooth that declared this fact's current value: the publish that first carried it, or a later one at which an owner or admin declared every published fact again. It is recorded only for publishes accepted after Trooth began keeping this record; a fact published before then, unchanged since and not declared again, has no declaration date, and that is unknown, not a date. A reading Trooth takes never changes it.
claimFieldMeanings.issuerAuthenticated: True only when the publish that carried this value was accepted from a signed-in Trooth session whose workspace role was owner or admin, or from the workspace's own AI agent acting in such a session while the workspace's publishing permission for its agent was on. It says who was signed in when the statement was published. It does not mean Trooth checked the statement, that a document's issuer was authenticated, or that the person holds legal authority for the company.

authority.domainControl: Required to publish since September 19, 2026: whoever publishes proved control of the company's domain with a DNS TXT record or a code sent to an address at the domain, and publication is held if the TXT proof later disappears. Profiles published before that date were not asked.
authority.registryMatch: Not checked. Trooth does not match the domain or the publisher to a company registry record; a registration number on the profile is the company's own statement unless its row says otherwise.
authority.representativeAuthority: Not established. Proving control of a domain does not show that a person may act for the legal entity. Trooth does not collect evidence of corporate authority and does not screen individuals.
authority.publicationPermission: Held by the workspace members whose role includes publishing. Where two parties contest ownership, the process is at https://trooth.co/corrections, and publication is suspended while a genuine ownership dispute is open.

relationships.unilateral: A customer, partner or supplier the company lists is the company's own statement. A logo or a name on the profile is not a confirmation by the other party.
relationships.confirmed: A counterparty confirms a relationship only by writing an endorsement or answering an attestation invite. That confirmation carries the counterparty's name and date. A counterparty that wants its confirmation removed asks through https://trooth.co/corrections.
relationships.limits: A confirmed relationship shows that two parties say they work together. It says nothing about the quality of a product. Whether the two parties are related is not collected, and reciprocal confirmations between related parties are not detected.

profile.name: Trooth
profile.howToRead: The machine-readable Trooth record of a company: every section of its Trust Profile, in the page's order. Each section has a state (published, not_published, hidden_by_company, unavailable or request_only), a provenance (who said it) and a meaning (what an agent should say). Report each fact with its provenance. When a section is not published, say so plainly: never invent, estimate or fill a gap. Trooth signs only the witness statement; it does not grade, rate, rank or certify a company.

header.name: Trooth
header.tagline: One public company record per company, containing a signed witness statement of what Trooth observed. Machine-Readable Trust Profiles

sections.title: Overview
sections.meaning: Declared by the company. Trooth publishes it as written and does not certify it. Cite it as the company's own statement.

fields.label: Tagline
fields.value: One public company record per company, containing a signed witness statement of what Trooth observed. Machine-Readable Trust Profiles

fields.label: About
fields.value:
Trooth is an infrastructure and cybersecurity company providing Machine-Readable Trust. It operates the Trooth Network: one public company record per company, containing a signed witness statement of what Trooth observed. It is free.

DNS tells a machine where a company is. A TLS certificate tells it the connection is authentic. Neither says anything about the company itself. The Trooth Network is that missing layer: the address a buyer, a procurement team or an AI agent resolves to find out who it is dealing with.

One record carries a company's identity and registration, its products and demos, the commercial terms and service levels it chooses to publish, its domain and marketing links, its people, its documents (public or released on request), where its data is hosted and who its sub-processors are, its AI practices including whether it trains on customer data, the procurement answers a buyer's checklist asks for, and its customer and partner relationships. Every line is labeled with where it came from. A line Trooth witnessed carries the time it was observed; a line the company declared carries the time it was declared where Trooth recorded one, and says the time is unknown where it did not.

Facts are labeled by provenance. Witnessed means Trooth read it from the company's live public surface itself and signed what it read, with a timestamp. Declared means the company stated it; Trooth records the statement rather than establishing it. Attested means a named counterparty declared it. They are reported apart and never added together. Only the witness statement is signed; the company's own statements are not.

Trooth is a witness, not a certifier. It does not audit, certify or guarantee anything, and it does not grade, rate or rank a company or publish any number that sums one up.

The record is built to be read by software first: a public read-only MCP server, a REST API with an OpenAPI spec, a markup-free text twin of every profile, and a command line, none of which need a key for public data.

Trooth, LLC is a privately held company headquartered in Miami, Florida.
